messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — Severity: P2. Multiple customer reports of 502/504s from azc (us-east-azc) behind ELB. Trigger: elevated 5xx rate, error budget burn > 15%. Paging oncall. Pager: @sre-amber

sre-amber: on it. seeing alerts from synthetic checks + spikes in ELB 502s ~ 10:07 UTC. Any current deploys?

eng-oncall: no deploys from platform in the last 30m, CI shows a canary finished 45m ago. Checking ELB target health now.

network-eli: I see weighted Route53 entries for the region shifting to azc due to weighted policy rebalance at ~10:05. Could be interacting with target group churn. Pulling Route53 logs.

prod-ops-miguel: customers seeing timeouts for streaming and chat endpoints. Error samples look like TLS handshake failures and occasional ECONNRESET from ELB->backend.

support-lin: incoming CS tickets narrow to EU clients hitting that region via our edge. Some show TCP resets mid-handshake.

eng-oncall: ELB backend health: two targets showing 502/503 recent, but they're in-service. CPU nominal. tail of app logs shows spike in short lived connection resets from nginx: "upstream prematurely closed connection"

network-eli: pulling VPC flow logs -> seeing increased SYN retries to instances from ELB IPs around 10:05-10:12. Might be network packet drops in azc hostplane.

incident-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1719287612. Current status: investigating. Channels: incidents (this thread), #postmortems (auto-created).

sre-amber: quick mitigation proposal: 1) shift Route53 weight off azc to other healthy AZs (reduce to 0% for a quick drain) 2) increase ELB connection timeout/backoff 3) cordon suspected hosts (if host-level net issues). I'll start the Route53 weight rollback.

eng-oncall: ack. Running: aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"azc","Weight":0}}]}'

deploy-bot: NOTE: Route53 change submitted, changeId: C1234567890. Estimated propagation 30s-90s.

network-eli: confirming NAT/ENI health: control plane shows ENI attach/retries on a subset of hosts in azc. Suspect underlying host networking driver flapping. Opening support case with AWS, will escalate.

prod-ops-miguel: scaling up cross-AZ capacity to handle shifted traffic, spinning additional instances in azb/aze. Will also warm cache/kv stores.

sre-amber: traffic shift in progress — seeing decrease in synthetic 502s after 40s. Still some client retries. Keep monitoring for residual 504s.

support-lin: telling CS to notify affected customers that we're mitigating and routing traffic away from the impacted AZ. Suggested message drafted.

eng-oncall: left a temporary ELB config change: healthcheck interval set to 10s -> more aggressive failover for bad backends. Also bumped max connection attempts.

network-eli: AWS case opened: "EC2 Elastic Network Interface intermittent attach/tx drops in us-east-azc". Case number 78901234. AWS response ETA 15m. Providing pcap and flow logs.

incident-bot: Update: incident severity remains P2. Postmortem owner assigned: @sre-amber.

sre-amber: handoff: @network-eli will continue AWS case and host remediation, @eng-oncall continue observing ELB health, @prod-ops-miguel to keep capacity and customer comms. I'll follow up for postmortem. If AWS confirms host-level flapping we'll plan a compensating action for dedicated pools.

prod-ops-miguel: CS notif sent to 12 affected accounts (low-latency tier). No billing impact expected.

eng-oncall: metrics: 5xx rate back down to baseline after full weight shift ~10:14. We'll keep ELB healthcheck change for 1hr then roll back.

network-eli: AWS replied: suspected NIC driver bug on host hypervisor causing transient packet drops; they've started instance isolation and are remediating fleet. They'll share final RCA.

support-lin: closing inbound tickets with note of mitigation and ETA for RCA.

sre-amber: closing this thread: mitigation successful, customer impact reduced. Postmortem scheduled for 48h. Thanks all, great triage. :thumbsup:
